speaker: Granny Gristle
before: "Went down in the muck, dearie, so we rolled you out. I'd charge you a mucking-out fee, but you've done the muck a favour. Heh!"
after: "You went down in the muck, my lovely, so we rolled you out. I'd charge you a mucking-out fee, but you've done the muck a favour. Hah!"

speaker: (narration)
before: You find a treasure chest among the rubbish. For once, sorting pays.
after: You find a treasure chest among the rubbish, which goes to show that sorting does pay now and then.

speaker: (narration)
before: You need a sack of fertilizer to plant a crop. The soil has standards. Low, fragrant standards.
after: You need a sack of fertilizer to plant a crop. The soil has standards, even if they are low and fragrant ones.

speaker: (narration)
before: A ripe harvest! Pumpkins, melons, one suspicious turnip.
after: A ripe harvest! You gather up pumpkins, melons and one suspicious turnip.

speaker: (narration)
before: The goat looks at you, looks at the pen, looks at the sign it was eating, and trots home. Round one: you.
after: The goat looks at you, looks at the pen, looks at the sign it was eating, and trots home, so round one goes to you.

speaker: (narration)
before: The pig is exactly where you expected, in the only puddle. A little shoving and it waddles home, offended.
after: The pig is exactly where you expected, in the only puddle, and after a little shoving it waddles home looking offended.

speaker: (narration)
before: The raccoon walks to the pen on its hind legs, tin can held like a briefcase. You appear to be its next appointment.
after: The raccoon walks to the pen on its hind legs with a tin can held like a briefcase, as if you were its next appointment.

speaker: (narration)
before: The seed cracks. The soil heaves. Green shoots race into the air, twisting and knotting...
after: The seed cracks, the soil heaves, and green shoots race up into the air, twisting and knotting as they go...

speaker: (narration)
before: You climb the beanstalk, hand over hand. The leaves are big enough to sit on. Do not sit on them.
after: You climb the beanstalk hand over hand, past leaves big enough to sit on, which is no reason to sit on them.

speaker: (narration)
before: You slide down the beanstalk. Leaf, leaf, leaf, ground. It is faster than the chute and much less dignified.
after: You slide down the beanstalk from leaf to leaf to leaf to ground, which is faster than the chute and much less dignified.

speaker: (narration)
before: You swing up onto the saddle. Faster, and it can smash junk barricades. Press Q to dismount.
after: You swing up onto the saddle. You move faster up here, and your mount can smash junk barricades. Press Q to dismount.

speaker: (narration)
before: You land in a pile of leaves. You decide not to examine the softer bits.
after: You land in a pile of leaves, and decide not to examine the softer bits.

speaker: Dump workers
before: If a raccoon in a crown asks for your lunch, say no. He'll cry. Still no.
after: If a raccoon in a crown asks for your lunch, say no, and keep saying no when he starts to cry.

speaker: Dump workers
before: The Buffet calls us garbage eaters. Half our garbage is their souffle, barely touched.
after: The Buffet calls us garbage eaters, but half our garbage is their souffle, and barely touched at that.

speaker: Dump workers
before: The beans came up purple again. I've stopped asking the beans.
after: The beans came up purple again. My mum grew beans for forty years and never saw the like.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Those purple trees were green last spring. Nobody's talking about it.
after: Those purple trees were green last spring, and I notice nobody wants to talk about it.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Stall's open! Patched awnings, patched prices. The holes are free.
after: Stall's open! The awnings are patched and so are the prices, and the holes come free.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Mind the vine ladders in the wind. They hold. Mostly.
after: Mind the vine ladders when the wind gets up. They'll hold you, mostly, but hang on with both hands.

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Found, not stolen, dearie! The raccoon found it. I just held on tight. Heh!
after: Found, not stolen, my lovely! The raccoon found it. I just held on tight. Hah!

speaker: Granny Gristle
before: Shed grew another room, dearie. At last, a growing business I don't have to water. Heh!
after: Born in a haybale, raised in a barn, my lovely, and I've never once paid full price.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: Every thought has a bin. Most of mine go in compost. That is not a complaint.
after: Every thought has its bin, and most of mine go in the compost, where they do some good.

speaker: Druid Thistlewick
before: The dishwasher talks back. I listen. Wisdom sometimes arrives with a rinse cycle.
after: Sit a while, if you like. Forty years I've sat here, and the fridges are good company.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: The vines have started whispering. Also, SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.
after: I think the vines have started whispering. And SOMEBODY ate the compost AGAIN.

speaker: Brother Bramble
before: Eleven little trees in a row, one per birthday. Then nobody came for the twelfth.
after: Eleven little trees in a row, one for each birthday, and nobody came for the twelfth.

speaker: (narration)
before: The roots have grown into the walls, the ceiling, the floor. Whatever lives here has eaten the light.
after: The roots have grown into the walls, the ceiling and the floor, and whatever lives down here has eaten the light.

speaker: (narration)
before: The wall pulses with warm, wet light. It is not entirely a wall.
after: The wall pulses with a warm, wet light, and you begin to suspect that it is not entirely a wall.

speaker: Dump workers
before: Every terrace a little greener. Even the top one. Especially the top one.
after: Every terrace is a little greener each morning, and the top one most of all, which nobody expected.
